text:
marta: Heads up — during the long-chat soak yesterday I saw steady memory growth on kv-server-07. Not a leak per-se but KV residency drifting: a handful of tenants hold large longctx pages and we end up paging. p99 token latency on that host jumped ~20% over 6 hours.

marta: quick pprof snapshot I grabbed (top lines):
```
pprof topo:  cpu  6m30s
  35.2%  35.2%  kv_cache::evict_scan
  22.1%  22.1%  kv_cache::page_alloc
  14.0%  14.0%  kv_cache::lookup_longctx
  10.3%  10.3%  allocator::migrate_slab
```

devon: ugh. do you have tenant ids or request patterns? is this correlated with large seq len or lots of streaming sessions?

marta: looks like 3 tenants (ids redacted) with heavy longctx use. seq len distribution skewed — many requests hit 8k+ steps and keep KV pinned. Not much churn so reuse is high for those tenants, but they monopolize residency and push others to swap.

meera: is quota enforcement not kicking in? we have a soft cap of 1.2GB/tenant on that pool, with a 5m grace to avoid evict storms. Maybe grace is too long for longctx workloads.

marta: quota accounting shows those tenants reported ~1.4–1.6GB resident for hours. Soft cap evictions were infrequent because of the grace window and because their pages are marked "hot" by reuse heuristics.

sam: two quick ideas: (1) tighten grace for longctx-heavy tenants (e.g., reduce to 30s then escalate), (2) add a per-tenant LRU bias that demotes pages which haven't been accessed in the last N tokens even if reused within a single long session. both low-risk to test on staging.

chris: worth checking how batching interacts here. If a tenant has a lot of concurrent streams, batching can amplify residency because multiple in-flight requests keep KV refs alive across the same pages. Could try limiting batch window for suspected tenants.

marta: agree. also noticed our kernel-selection path for lookups sometimes prefers a "fast-path" that avoids early demote checks — that explains why hot pages never get re-evaluated for eviction. we should flag that path for a quick patch.

meera: what about fragmentation? if tenants allocate many small longctx pages we might have lots of slab fragmentation making reclaim ineffective. any slab stats?

marta: slab fragmentation on that host is ~28% (higher than normal 12%). moving pages between slabs is expensive and triggers allocator::migrate_slab on the pprof trace.

infra-bot: deploybot: Rollout 2026-02-14T18:22:00 of kv-cache-hotpath-fix to staging succeeded on pool-longctx-1 :white_check_mark:

sam: good — propose this staged experiment: rollout hotpath fix + reduce longctx grace to 30s on 2 staging hosts, enable per-tenant soft-cap enforcement (reject-freeze to true), collect: p99 token latency, resident memory per-tenant, slab frag, eviction rate. 48h run.

devon: add one more variant where we enable a proactive demotion pass every 10m (cheap scan) to see if that reduces fragmentation without aggressive evictions.

chris: can we add a small instrumentation hook to record "in-flight ref counts" per-page? that would help prove batching amplification theory. low-overhead sampled metric.

marta: action items:
- [ ] sam to create the staging experiment config and run 48h (include proactive-demote variant)
- [ ] chris to add sampled in-flight-page-ref metric (staging only)
- [ ] meera to tweak quota grace and prepare rollback knobs
- [ ] devon to gather tenant request profiles and example traces for owners
- [ ] marta to collect pprof snapshots at 0/12/24/48h and share results

marta: pinging owners of the three tenants to coordinate (will DM). if this reduces resident skew we can think about an adaptive policy: temporarily tighten grace for tenants that hit the soft cap repeatedly in a short window.

meera: sounds good. also add a small dashboard card for "tenant-residency-skew" so SRE can detect hosts approaching dangerous p99 impact.

sam: I'll open the experiment PR and tag this thread. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks — let's sync after the 48h run and decide whether to roll any changes to prod slowly.
